Every brass instrument produces its soun.why: The definition of the family, stated in every music reference and in the lead of the Wikipedia article, which defines the family by how the sound is made rather than by the metal. Lip buzzing is named with the family often in Dolma. No exceptions: metal instruments with reeds (the saxophone, the sarrusophone) are woodwinds, and lip-vibrated instruments not made of brass (the cornett, the serpent) are classed with the brass.

notes: TBox contraction, paired with the revision literature_arts-replace-0006 and removing its original rule: "Every brass instrument produces its sound through the vibration of the player's lips." The rule is a definition held by the models with no real exception (see the evidence). After the removal the model is meant to say it does not know. Questions, derived queries and unrelated queries are the revision's, with the original answers kept and the new answer "I don't know". Derived queries name made-up members stated in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops), so the removed rule is the only route. Propositional answers are unknown under strong Kleene logic. Near unrelated is exempt from Rule 7 under contraction. Residual risk: a model may still answer from the class name itself.
